items.prompt: Explain how agricultural employment can rise while its share falls using invented totals: Year 1 agriculture 200/services 300; Year 2 agriculture 220/services 380.
items.canonical_answer: Agriculture rises 20, but total employment rises 500 to 600 as services grow faster. Agriculture’s share falls from 40% to about 36.67%; its level and share therefore move differently.
marking_guidance: Starting change (1): Agricultural jobs rise from 200 to 220.
Because/mechanism (1): Total jobs rise from 500 to 600 as services grow faster.
Mechanism development (1): Agriculture’s share falls from 40% to about 36.67%.
Consequence (1): A falling share is compatible with a rising employment level.
items.repair_note: Jeremy-authorised repairs for Claude review 6145-AUTH-R1: terminology, central-bank functions, precise definitions, specific credit points and misconception discrimination.

items.prompt: Explain the denominator for an invented unemployment rate with 600 employed, 100 unemployed under the stated definition and 300 residents outside the labour force.
items.canonical_answer: The labour force is 600 + 100 = 700, so the rate is 100/700, about 14.29%. The 300 outside the labour force are excluded.
marking_guidance: Context (1): employed plus unemployed denominator. Reason/conclusion (1): rate about 14.29%, excluding others.

items.prompt: Explain unemployment where a broad fall in orders leads firms to cut output and dismiss workers whose skills remain suitable.
items.canonical_answer: Reduced demand for products reduces the output firms plan to sell. Their derived demand for labour falls, creating demand-deficient unemployment despite suitable worker skills.
marking_guidance: Because/mechanism (1): Firms reduce planned saleable production.
Mechanism development (1): Derived demand for labour falls.
Consequence (1): Demand-deficient unemployment can rise despite suitable skills.
items.repair_note: Jeremy-authorised repairs for Claude review 6145-AUTH-R1: terminology, central-bank functions, precise definitions, specific credit points and misconception discrimination.

items.prompt: Explain the unemployment cause where new technician vacancies exist but displaced manual workers lack the required skill.
items.canonical_answer: This is structural skill mismatch. Vacancies do not provide employment to those workers immediately because their skills do not meet the new job requirements.
marking_guidance: Context (1): vacancies and unsuitable skills. Reason/conclusion (1): structural mismatch limits access.

items.prompt: Explain how prolonged unemployment can affect a household with no replacement earnings and limited savings.
items.canonical_answer: Lost earnings reduce available spending funds. Limited savings can cushion only some costs; continued unemployment can force cuts and hardship and may weaken skills or recruitment prospects over time.
marking_guidance: Starting change (1): Unemployment removes earned income.
Because/mechanism (1): Limited savings can cushion only some commitments.
Mechanism development (1): Spending cuts or hardship can follow without replacement earnings.
Consequence (1): Long duration can also weaken skills or later recruitment prospects.

items.prompt: Explain why closure of a plant with 30 jobs is not evidence that all 30 remain unemployed when 20 affected workers find other work in the same period.
items.canonical_answer: The closure is a gross job loss, while subsequent employment offsets part of it. The net unemployment effect differs, although replacement pay, hours and transition costs still matter.
marking_guidance: Context (1): re-employment of 20. Reason/conclusion (1): distinguish gross loss from net unemployment.

items.prompt: Evaluate training as the main remedy where unemployed workers lack the skills for genuine unfilled vacancies, but courses take time and some workers cannot easily attend.
items.canonical_answer: Relevant training addresses the mismatch and can improve access to vacancies. Time and attendance barriers limit the response, and jobs must remain available. Support targeted accessible training under those conditions; broad demand support alone does not supply the missing skill.
marking_guidance: Argument for (2): skill acquired (1), access to genuine jobs (1). Argument against (2): time (1), attendance barrier (1). Condition (1): relevant accessible training and sustained vacancies. Judgement (2): targeted training supported (1), matched to cause (1). Total 7.

items.prompt: Define unemployment (2). Identify causes in two invented cases: broad weak orders with suitable workers; vacancies requiring skills workers lack (2). Explain one consequence of lost work where there is no replacement income (2). Identify a remedy matched to each of those causes (2).
items.canonical_answer: Unemployment concerns people without work, willing and able to work and seeking employment under the measure. The causes are demand deficiency and structural mismatch. Lost earnings reduce purchasing power. Feasible demand support addresses weak orders; relevant training addresses the skill gap.
marking_guidance: Meaning (2): without work (1), willing/able/seeking under measure (1). Separate points for causes (2): demand deficiency (1), structural mismatch (1). Explanation (2): earnings lost (1), reduced spending capacity (1). Remedies (2): demand support (1), relevant training (1). Marks allocation 8.

items.prompt: Invented district: total employment rises 500 to 600, with agriculture 200 to 220 and services 300 to 380. Group A workers lose jobs after a broad fall in orders despite suitable skills and spare capacity. Group B cannot fill genuine technician vacancies because training is missing. Both groups lose earned income; savings are limited. Funded demand support and relevant accessible training are feasible, but each uses resources and training takes time. Describe three employment/cause features, each with a detail (6). Explain the distinct unemployment mechanisms and consequences for earnings and spending (7). Discuss demand support versus training for these groups (7).
items.canonical_answer: Agricultural jobs rise but share falls; A has demand-deficient unemployment; B has structural mismatch. Weak orders reduce output and labour demand for A, while missing skills prevent B accessing existing vacancies. Lost earnings reduce spending where savings are limited. Demand support is more direct for A, training for B; cost, time and sustained suitable vacancies condition the combination.
marking_guidance: Data description (6): changing agriculture share/level (1), 200 to 220 with faster total growth detail (1); demand cause A (1), weak orders detail (1); mismatch B (1), missing technician skill detail (1). Mechanism/explanation (7): weak orders (1), output cut (1), labour demand falls (1); vacancies exist (1), B lacks required skill (1); earnings lost (1), limited savings weaken spending (1). Both sides/judgement (7): demand support creates A orders (1), training equips B (1); demand alone not B skill solution (1), training alone not A customer solution (1); condition cost/time and actual capacity/vacancies (1); judgement matched combination (1), group-specific reason (1). Marks allocation 6+7+7=20.

facts: Invented district: total employment rises 500 to 600, with agriculture 200 to 220 and services 300 to 380. Group A workers lose jobs after a broad fall in orders despite suitable skills and spare capacity. Group B cannot fill genuine technician vacancies because training is missing. Both groups lose earned income; savings are limited. Funded demand support and relevant accessible training are feasible, but each uses resources and training takes time.

items.prompt: Invented cases. Case 1: genuine technician vacancies exist, but unemployed workers lack the relevant skill; accessible funded training takes six months. Case 2: a general demand fall has reduced orders, while unemployed workers retain suitable skills and capacity is idle; funded purchases can start, but imports absorb part of spending. No general skill shortage is stated in Case 2. Evaluate relevant training versus demand support in Case 1 (7). Evaluate those remedies in Case 2 (7).
items.canonical_answer: Case 1: training directly fills the skill gap, though six months delays employment and vacancies must persist; demand support alone does not create the qualification. Case 2: purchases directly support weak orders and use idle capacity, though imports and funding limit the effect; training does not directly repair the stated lack of demand. Choose the remedy matching each cause with its implementation conditions.
marking_guidance: Case 1 marks (7): argument for skill remedy (1), existing vacancies (1); argument against six-month delay (1), vacancy persistence uncertain (1); condition relevant successful training (1); judgement training priority (1), demand alone not skill solution (1). Case 2 allocation (7): argument for orders (1), idle resources respond (1); argument against import content (1), funding/implementation costs (1); condition domestic response and affordability (1); judgement demand support priority (1), training alone not stated cause remedy (1). Total 14.
